findings.finding: A $150M at-the-market program with TD Securities (8-K and S-3ASR, 2026-06-18) is open and can sell stock into any bounce on 2026-10-14. Sales are disclosed only in the next 10-Q.
findings.mechanism_in_window: An ATM sells at market on any session, including 2026-10-14. The company needs no new filing to draw it, so it acts as live overhead supply inside the window rather than a later event.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tickeron attributed the 2026-07-16 fall of -17.57% partly to dilution worries after the shelf filing. That is a secondary, weakly sourced attribution. The baseline's own falls since July show next-close continuation on 7 of 12.
findings.why_not_priced: The ATM is public, so its existence is priced. What the price cannot see is whether the company is drawing it. If ATM supply were the seller today, the tape would look like this: steady falls on ordinary volume with no news. That fits, but it is an inference with no disclosure behind it.

findings.finding: Management met investors at an Oppenheimer-hosted meeting in New York on the drop day, 2026-10-13. Per stockanalysis's event list, it puts a sell-side counterparty in front of the stock as it falls.
findings.mechanism_in_window: Any note or reiteration from the Oppenheimer meeting would land before or during the 2026-10-14 session. That is unconfirmed. Coverage is uniformly Buy (HC Wainwright $60, BTIG $55, Guggenheim and TD Cowen initiations in September).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The September conference and initiation run (Guggenheim and TD Cowen Buy initiations, about 2026-09-15/16) did not stop the slide: the stock fell from about $39 to about $33 that week.
findings.why_not_priced: Today's tape was traders with no news. Any defence from the meeting would reach a wider audience overnight. The finding is small because recent Buy initiations demonstrably did not reverse the trend.
